notes:
• Fallout 2d20: the HUD can be enabled in a Fallout world. The interface, chat, carousel and scene bar work as in any system, and the carousel reads a Fallout character's health. There is no projection: with Scorpious187's Pip-Boy active, the device's switch brings up the Pip-Boy instead, for the player's own character, or for the GM the selected token's (a character or a robot), and follows the GM's selection as the projection does. Closing the Pip-Boy turns the device off, and switching the device off puts the Pip-Boy away, even one that is still opening, or whose opening failed part way.
  • Fallout 2d20: the Pip-Boy Lonestar Edition, a look of its own over the omni-tool: the Pip-Boy's olive forearm unit, with its amber POWER lamp, lit while the device is on, as the switch, and the interface in the Pip-Boy's phosphor green. Everyone wears it in a Fallout world, where the device settings are hidden, and it is offered in no other system.
  • Fallout 2d20: the system's AP tracker rides on the device, Overseer AP to the left of the macro bar and Party AP to the right, in the device's colors, and the device widens to carry them. It had been left loose in the page, where it pushed the sidebar in from the edge of the screen.
  • Fallout 2d20: chat cards are drawn on the device's panels without the system's paper underneath, which had left them light text on a light page. A roll's successes, complications and damage are cells edged in green, red and yellow, in the device's letters, and the card's title is sized for the chat log.
  • The carousel turns smoothly. A card that has not changed is no longer drawn again, so its portrait does not reload. A redraw part way through a turn no longer starts the slide over. The card going around from one end of the row to the other leaves off its edge and comes in at the other, instead of crossing the whole row. The round marker slides with the cards, and a card whose turn starts or ends grows or shrinks as it moves.

Full details in the release notes.
